(3) For the purpose of recovering khas possession of any property under-sub-section (2), the District Magistrate may use or cause to be used such force as may be necessary for the purpose of evicting any such person at the request of the Court. 

 (4) No Civil Court shall entertain any suit or legal proceedings concerning any matter relating to the recovery of khas possession of any property under this section or pass in ay such suit or proceeding an order granting temporary or interim injunction restraining the Court from taking possession of any such property. 

 33. We have scrutinized the said section and found that the section is applicable in case of the property remained in charge of the court of wards and if the said property is transferred by the court of wards to some third party by sale, gift or by any other modes of transfer, then for giving delivery of possession of such transferred property to said transferee, the court of wards can exercise such power of eviction as stated. Section 18(A) was inserted in the Court of Wards Act after SAT Act. 1950, stating that, the court of wards can keep in its charge only the retainable khas land after acquisitioning rent receiving interest of the rent receiver over its projabili property by the Government under SAT Act, 1950. The petitioners property appertaining to C.S Khatian No. 7 having found at page 492 of projabill property Gazette, it can never be in-charge of the Court of Wards and claiming title therein by the Court of Wards would be another contempt of court as per judgment of the High Court Division as well as Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Bangladesh. It may be further stated that in its written statements, had never claimed suit property appertaining to C.S. khatian No.7 as of its own property, rather claimed as property of private deity of Sree Sree Madhab Bigraha and said Bigraha got decree in Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985, through its so called shebayet Abdur Rod, the Manager, Court of Wards, on 24.10.1996
